A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Geometry-aware 4D Video Generation for Robot Manipulation. All 23 pages, including Appendices A.1–A.7, support comparison; text comparison and rendered-page inspection confirm matching scientific content, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-generation experiments and robot-policy success rates in Section 4, plus pose-tracking and three-view evaluations in Appendices A.6–A.7.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices, including Tables 1–4 and Figure 13.

M1.justification: The SVD-based RGB/pointmap model, cross-view attention, training losses, and FoundationPose trajectory extraction are identical. The gripper-weighted loss and additional-view inference procedure already appear in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three simulation tasks, four real-world tasks, and novel camera viewpoints. The three-view StoreCerealBoxUnderShelf evaluation in Appendix A.7 is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains OURS w/o MV attn, 4D Gaussian, SVD, and SVD w/ MV attn. Table 2 retains Dreamitate, Diffusion Policy, and DP3; comparator membership and descriptions are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both specify identical camera splits, dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, training settings, and 30 policy rollouts per task. The pose-tracking control and three-view evaluation protocols in Appendices A.6–A.7 also match.

E4.justification: The cross-attention ablation, qualitative comparisons, ground-truth RGB-D pose-tracking error analysis, and additional-view scaling analysis are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including averaging across initial conditions in Appendix A.7. Neither version reports training-seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the qualitative results match. For example, Table 2 reports identical proposed-method success rates of 0.73, 0.67, and 0.53, averaging 0.64; Figure 13 retains the same pose-error curves and examples.

T1.justification: The pointmap definitions and mathematical objectives in Equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric and temporal consistency, generalization to novel viewpoints, and extracting manipulation trajectories from generated RGB-D videos.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of cross-attention benefits and baseline failures, alongside limitations involving RGB-D data collection and slow inference. Appendix discussions of efficiency, pose-tracking errors, and three-view degradation also match.

D1.justification: Architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, sampling procedures, and computational costs remain identical in the main text and appendices. Section 8 retains the same project information and prospective code, dataset, and model release statement.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list retain the same works and research positioning. Colored citation links in v4 do not change their substance.

P1.justification: v4 corrects 'braintorming' to 'brainstorming' in the acknowledgments, adds the ICLR 2026 publication header, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 introduces green citation links, red internal-reference links, magenta external links, and a running conference header. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–4 retain their content, structure, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and appendix analyses are unchanged. The spelling correction, publication metadata, and hyperlink coloring are limited presentation edits that do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
